timeline.label: Quarter ended with $48.7 million cash, $17 thousand of notes payable, and only $173 thousand of land-sale revenue.
Fiscal year revenue $52.8 million. About 16,200 acres still owned in Sandoval County, including about 15,300 undeveloped acres.
Adrienne M. Uleau became chief financial officer in July 2025 after serving as controller and vice president of finance.
Defined-benefit pension terminated. Residual $547 thousand moved into the 401(k) and is restricted cash, not a pension liability.
Worthless-stock deduction on Palm Coast Data Holdco, the former fulfillment subsidiary, produced a large tax loss that still supports part of the federal loss carryforward.
Bought 2,096,061 shares (28.6%) from the Karabots estate and related companies at $10.45, below the prior close of $11.47.
Chief executive Christopher V. Vitale received an option for 50,000 shares at $14.24, exercisable November 1, 2026 if still employed.
Christopher V. Vitale became president and chief executive. He has been a director since 2021.
Last fiscal year in which the company paid a cash dividend, per the fiscal 2026 10-K.
Organized in Oklahoma. The land business is concentrated in Rio Rancho and adjoining Sandoval County.

industry.structure: Rio Rancho land sales are competitive and concentrated. In fiscal 2026 every developed residential acre AMREP sold went to three homebuilders. Homebuilding competes with national, regional, and local builders plus resale and rental housing.
industry.share_shift: AMREP slowed its own lot pipeline and put more effort into its homebuilding segment. Starts in Rio Rancho by all builders fell from 973 in fiscal 2025 to 805 in fiscal 2026.
industry.trend: Higher mortgage rates and house prices have paused buyers. The company cut some prices, offered incentives, leased finished homes, and delayed projects because of entitlement and utility delays. It tells owners to expect lower developed-lot revenue in fiscal 2027.
